Save plan appends claimed, commits one savedPlan whose id is the claim's, whose decided is the claim record's HLC and whose stamp is .planSave(c) with the claim's attempt and the confirmation's account, then appends saved and answers .saved. plan_load returns that object byte for byte. Cancel appends canceled and writes no plan; the saved plan before it is unchanged. Saving plan B after A makes plan_load return B, and memory_query shows the A to B line. Each card's "replaces" line names the saved plan that was newest when its confirmation ended, and a card that has not ended names the newest saved plan now. A waiting card, carried ones included, follows a plan saved after it was prepared. A waiting card names the newest saved plan even when another device decided it after the card's ten minutes by its own clock. A Saving or Saved card names the newest plan decided before its claim, never its own. A Canceled card names the newest plan decided before its cancel, a replaced card the newest decided before the next prepared step, the one that replaced it and not a later one, even when that card is saved only after the replaced card's ten minutes, and an expired card the newest decided before the instant it reads Expired, whichever of replacement and expiry came first, even when its prepared step's HLC ran ahead of the clock. A plan decided at that instant is not on the line, one decided a millisecond before it or earlier within that millisecond is, and a replacement prepared at that same instant leaves the expiry as the end. The line compares and orders plans by when they were decided, not by when their records arrived. No such plan means no line: saving A leaves A's card with none, and after B is saved, B names A and A still has none.
A newer prepared in the same conversation makes the older one .replaced: its card reads Expired with no controls, and Save on it answers .notSaved(.replaced) and writes nothing.

When settle's append of card 2 runs between card 1's read and its claim append, card 1's Save answers .notSaved(.replaced) and no savedPlan row exists.

With HeldClock, after waitUntilHeld(.seconds(600)) for the settle's wake: advanced 599 seconds, Save saves. In a second run advanced exactly 600 seconds, the wake yields changes, the card reads Expired with no controls, Save answers .notSaved(.expired), and the record count does not change.
After the phone switches to another athlete, Save answers .notSaved(.athleteChanged) and writes nothing.

After New conversation, a waiting card is shown once at the top as preparedEarlier, keeps its armed controls, and Cancel works; it then reads Canceled at the top until the next New conversation. A carried card whose ten minutes end reads Expired at the top until the next New conversation, and is not shown after that. No card is carried for a confirmation saved or canceled before the reset, one whose ten minutes ended before the reset, or one that is not the newest. At the edge, one whose ten minutes end exactly at the reset boundary is not carried, and one prepared a second later is carried. The ten minutes run from the prepared step's HLC wall time, so a step that ran ahead of the clock is carried past its expiry and reads Expired at the top.

A storage failure after the claim answers .storageUnavailable, marks that card storageUnavailable, and records planSaveStalled. Meanwhile another confirmation is prepared and saved, and its card reads Saved.
No step of a save or a cancel calls the calendar. Approving a workout review saves no plan and leaves the saved plan unchanged.
With HeldClock, a workout review waiting more than ten minutes beside a plan-save confirmation stays approvable after the confirmation expires.
A second device that shares the synced store sees the saved plan in its prompt and plan_load, and no card and no control.
Choosing a coaching option while a card waits saves no plan and writes no claim.

With plan A saved, one turn calls build_plan_skeleton twice, a draft and then a revision, and get_sample_week, and replies. Then plan_load returns A byte for byte, the raw savedPlan row count is unchanged, no card and no planConfirmation record exists, and FakeIntervalsClient.calls is empty.
ChatSnapshot.plans reaches the app through Coach, and the public-surface fixtures list Coach.decide(_: PlanDecision, in:) and ChatSnapshot.plans.
make check-source fails ClaimedSave( outside PlanSave.swift, LiveConfirmation( outside PlanConfirmation.swift and PlanSaveToken( outside PlanCard.swift, each with a passing and a failing case.

SlashRouting.parse("/plan for my gran fondo in June") is .plan and its route is .modelTurn, and the slash list and the welcome list /plan after /workout with "Generate a training plan" in every catalog language.
Sending /plan for my gran fondo in June stores and sends that text unchanged, and the transcript shows the athlete's message and the coach's progress with no acknowledgement row.
A user message whose command is /plan is stored at body version 7, above the version 6 a Milestone 4 build reads, so that build skips it as newerVersion, and every other user message keeps version 4.
A fixture-transport /plan turn offers build_plan_skeleton, assess_feasibility and get_sample_week, and its system prompt and tools equal those of the same turn sent as plain text.
/plan with no usable model access settles with the existing access failure and its notice, makes no model request, and shows no card, confirmation or saved plan.

requirements.statement: Fixtures that compare npm and phone outputs are made by a committed generator from npm at d192cb974e715e1527645e0acf0d8353ed4d0edc, refuse any other revision, Node or checkout state, and are checked against their manifest on every make test-swift.
A saved plan is retained across installed-app updates: a saved plan committed into a store a Milestone 4 build wrote reads back whole after the store is opened again.

Versioned storage keeps a saved plan's meaning across an upgrade: a saved plan is stored at body version 7, a later version is skipped rather than misread, and an older build's store opens with every row intact.

The coach gets the saved plan's four-line headline in every prompt and the whole plan through plan_load, and never a plan that does not exist: with none saved, the prompt says "No plan saved yet." and plan_load answers so.
Saves and replacements of the saved plan show in memory_query history with was and now previews, apart from workout reviews and unsaved plan-save confirmations.
plan_save refuses a plan whose plan_load result would not fit the tool-result cap.
requirements.agreedDifference: ADR-0084 refuses a plan whose plan_load result would not fit the tool-result cap, the same rule the runtime applies to every tool result; npm has no limit. Shown by 5.1.4.

requirements.statement: The saved plan text sorts its keys; npm keeps the order the model sent.
requirements.agreedDifference: ADR-0084 saves the plan text with sorted keys, where npm keeps the order the model sent; the values are the same. Shown by 5.1.2.

requirements.statement: The phone's day in the phone's time zone decides a plan draft's week count.
requirements.agreedDifference: ADR-0083 and ADR-0084: build_plan_skeleton counts weeks to the race from the phone's day in the phone's time zone, where npm counts from the time zone its host passes to the tool. Shown by 4.1.5.

requirements.statement: A turn that committed plan-save work is never replayed: a prepared confirmation counts as saved work, so Try again is refused after it, and a held plan_save that was never stored does not stop a retry.
A step-limit summary reply keeps its plan-save confirmation.
requirements.agreedDifference: ADR-0084: a turn that reaches the step limit and then replies with its summary, or with the catalog's fallback when the summary is empty, ends well and keeps its confirmation. Shown by 6.3.5.

requirements.statement: No plan is saved for a turn with no usable athlete on this device.
requirements.agreedDifference: ADR-0084: plan_save answers plan_unavailable and holds nothing for an unconnected turn on a device that connected before, where npm saves for whatever athlete its host passes. Shown by 6.3.10.

requirements.statement: Two plan_save calls in one step are both refused.
requirements.agreedDifference: ADR-0084: two plan_save calls in one step both answer concurrent_plan_save and every later plan_save of the attempt is refused, where npm runs each call. Shown by 6.3.3.

requirements.statement: Choosing a coaching option is never plan-save approval: it saves no plan and writes no claim while a plan-save card waits.

Across New conversation, a plan-save confirmation follows its own rule: only the newest one with no decision before the reset and whose ten minutes end after it is carried to the top, and it is gone after the next New conversation.
Each durable plan record follows its own rule across New conversation: the saved plan stays saved, and a carried confirmation keeps its controls until it is decided or its ten minutes end.
Synced history never grants plan-save approval on another device: a second device sees the saved plan in its prompt and plan_load, and no card and no control.

/plan shows no separate acknowledgement: npm's Telegram reply "Analyzing your data and building a plan..." has no phone counterpart, and the transcript shows only the athlete's message, the coach's progress and the reply.
requirements.agreedDifference: ADR-0084 returns /plan as Generate a training plan with no acknowledgement shown; 7.2.2 shows the transcript with none.

requirements.statement: Text typed after /plan reaches the coach: npm's Telegram /plan sends the literal "/plan", while the phone stores and sends the whole message as typed.
requirements.agreedDifference: ADR-0084 and D09 forward the text after /plan; 7.2.2 shows the message stored and sent unchanged.
